title: Characterizing Protein–Protein Interactions Using OpenSPR
author: Cassie Shu Zhu

steps.title: Set up instrument and fluidics
steps.instruction: Connect the OpenSPR instrument to the computer via USB, install the three buffer bottles (HBS‑T, waste, and optional extra) as described in the manual, open the Experiment Data Interface and click Start.

steps.title: Load NTA sensor chip
steps.instruction: Clean the Flow Cell face with a lint‑free wipe soaked in 80 % isopropanol and let air‑dry, rinse the NTA Sensor Chip with distilled water and air‑dry, then slide the chip into the Sensor Holder in the correct orientation and insert the holder into the instrument, aligning it with the Fluidics Block.

steps.title: Rinse and purge injection lines
steps.instruction: Switch the Injection Valve to the Load position, then slowly rinse the Injection Port and Sample Loop with at least 1.0 mL of running buffer (HBS‑T, pH 7.4) to flush previous solutions, followed by purging the Sample Loop with at least 1.0 mL of air using a buffer syringe to remove excess liquid and bubbles.

steps.title: Remove bubbles with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Set the pump speed to 150 μL/min, keep the Injection Valve in the Load position, inject 300 μL of 80 % isopropanol via a blunt‑end syringe into the Sample Loop, then turn the Injection Valve clockwise to the Inject position to deliver isopropanol to the sensor, and finally return the valve to the Load position.

steps.title: Condition surface with imidazole
steps.instruction: Set pump speed to 150 μL/min, fill the 100 μL Sample Loop with 200 μL of 200 mM imidazole solution (prepared with the NTA Reagent Kit), turn the Injection Valve to Inject to flow imidazole over the sensor for 5 min, then return the valve to Load. Rinse the Inject Port and Sample Loop with ≥1.0 mL HBS‑T and purge with ≥1.0 mL air as in step 3.

steps.title: Activate NTA surface with NiCl2
steps.instruction: Set pump speed to 20 μL/min, fill the Sample Loop with 200 μL of 40 mM NiCl₂ solution (NTA Reagent Kit), switch the Injection Valve to Inject and deliver NiCl₂ to the sensor until a stable baseline is obtained, then return the valve to Load. Rinse the Inject Port and Sample Loop with ≥1.0 mL HBS‑T and purge with ≥1.0 mL air.

steps.title: Switch running buffer to PBS
steps.instruction: In the Pump Menu, click Stop, switch the inlet tubing from the HBS‑T bottle to the 1× PBS bottle (pH 7.4, catalog NI‑PBS), then click Start to resume pumping.

steps.title: Immobilize pCTS‑L ligand
steps.instruction: Set pump speed to 20 μL/min, load a disposable syringe with a gastight blunt‑end tip with 200 μL of pCTS‑L solution diluted in 1× PBS to a final concentration of 50 μg/mL, inject the solution into the Sample Loop, quickly turn the Injection Valve clockwise to Inject, and leave the valve in the Inject position for the entire ligand‑binding period until the sensorgram reaches a plateau (optional repeat immobilization to ensure maximal capture).

steps.title: Stabilize baseline before analyte
steps.instruction: Allow the instrument to run with 1× PBS until the baseline slope is < 5 pM/min (typically 5 min to 1 h). Then rinse the Inject Port and Sample Loop with running buffer (1× PBS) and purge with air as in step 3.

steps.title: Inject TLR4 analyte series
steps.instruction:
Prepare TLR4 analyte in 1× PBS at 3‑fold serial dilutions: 31.5 nM, 94.6 nM, and 283.7 nM. For each concentration (increasing order):
1. Load a syringe with 200 μL of the analyte, insert it into the Injection Port, depress the plunger slowly, wait ≥5 s for pressure stabilization, then remove the syringe.
2. Turn the Injection Valve clockwise to Inject, deliver the sample at 20 μL/min for an association time of 240 s.
3. When the Injection Remaining counter reaches 00:00:00, turn the Valve back to Load and allow dissociation for 480 s.
4. After the baseline has settled, rinse the Inject Port and Sample Loop with 1× PBS and purge with air as in step 3 before the next concentration.
5. Input the ligand name (TLR4) and concentration in the Injection Details box for data tracking.

steps.title: Finalize and save experiment
steps.instruction: When all TLR4 injections are complete and the baseline has stabilized, click Finish in the software to stop tracking the absorbance peak and generate the final data files (saved under Documents\OpenSPR\TestResults\ with the user‑provided experiment name).

steps.title: Prepare RAGE analyte series
steps.instruction: Load a new NTA Sensor Chip (repeat steps 1‑7), prepare RAGE analyte in 1× PBS at 3‑fold serial dilutions: 27.7 nM, 83.3 nM, and 250 nM, and inject each 200 μL sample at 20 μL/min with 240 s association and 480 s dissociation, following the same procedure as for TLR4 (steps 8‑10).

steps.title: Analyze data in TraceDrawer
steps.instruction: Open TraceDrawer software, click Add Run to import the saved OpenSPR files, create a new Overlay and drag the runs onto it, then click New Evaluation, set Evaluation Type to Kinetics, define the two timepoints marking the start and end of the association phase, assign the corresponding concentrations for each curve, choose the OneToOne model (diffusion‑corrected, global fitting) and press Fit. Use the software’s manual for additional display or axis adjustments if desired.

steps.title: Shutdown and clean fluidic lines
steps.instruction: If the instrument will not be used soon, perform a full shutdown: rinse all fluidic lines with at least 20 mL of deionized water followed by at least 20 mL of 80 % isopropanol at the maximum pump speed (150 μL/min), then purge the lines with sufficient air to dry the tubing.
